name: Grove gas voltaic battery
description: Grove described a gas voltaic battery that produced electricity from hydrogen and oxygen.

impact.note: One laboratory demonstration with no practical use at the time, yet the whole later line of fuel-cell work traces back to it.

places.note: Place refers to the sourced event; historic political boundaries are not inferred.

date.label: October 1842
date.basis: Date stated in the cited source.

events.statement: In an October 1842 letter to Faraday, Grove described his completed gas voltaic battery.

evidence.locator: Grove’s gas battery and October 1842 letter
evidence.supports: APS reproduces an excerpt of Grove’s 1842 letter reporting a completed gas voltaic battery using hydrogen and oxygen; its account distinguishes this from his separate acid-based Grove cell.

events.caveats: The cited historical account reproduces a letter excerpt; this is an experimental device, not a commercial power supply.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest event for this scoped capability established by the inspected passages; no global priority is inferred.

unresolved.note: The account describes earlier electrolysis and a separate Grove cell but does not establish a causal link to a particular represented experimental apparatus.
